questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a transition element?
questions.explain: Zn has a full d subshell both in the ground state (3d¹⁰4s²) and in its common oxidation state (Zn²⁺, 3d¹⁰). So it is not a transition element.

questions.q: What is the ground-state configuration of Cr (Z = 24)?
questions.explain: A half-filled d⁵ subshell is more stable, so one electron moves from 4s to 3d.

questions.q: Which element of the first (3d) series shows the largest number of oxidation states?
questions.explain: Mn shows +2 to +7 — it has the most unpaired d electrons, in the middle of the series.

questions.q: What is the spin-only magnetic moment of Mn²⁺?
How many unpaired electrons does Ni²⁺ (3d⁸) have, and what is μ?
questions.explain: 3d⁸ has 3 pairs and 2 unpaired electrons; μ = √(2 × 4) = 2.84 BM.

questions.q: Which of these ions is colourless in aqueous solution?
questions.explain: Sc³⁺ = d⁰ — a d–d transition is not possible, so it is colourless. The others have partly filled d subshells.

questions.q: Why is Cu⁺ unstable in aqueous solution?
options: It disproportionates, 2Cu⁺ → Cu²⁺ + Cu, because the hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺ is much more negative
Cu⁺ has a very high charge
questions.explain: The high hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺ makes up for the second ionisation enthalpy of Cu, so Cu²⁺ is more stable.

questions.q: Why is the enthalpy of atomisation of Zn (126 kJ mol⁻¹) the lowest in the first series?
options: Zn is 3d¹⁰ — no unpaired electrons, so the interatomic interaction is weak
The oxidation state of Zn is +1
questions.explain: Many unpaired d electrons make interatomic bonding strong; Zn has none.

questions.q: Why does Cu not liberate H₂ from dilute HCl?
options: The oxidation state of Cu is +3
questions.explain: With a positive E° the metal is a weaker reducing agent than H₂; it cannot reduce H⁺.

questions.q: What is the colour change when alkali (OH⁻) is added to an orange K₂Cr₂O₇ solution?
questions.explain: Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 2OH⁻ → 2CrO₄²⁻ + H₂O; chromate is yellow. The oxidation state of Cr (+6) stays the same.

questions.q: In the reduction of KMnO₄ in acidic medium, how many electrons does manganese gain, and what is the product?
questions.explain: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O (E° = +1.52 V). The oxidation number of Mn goes from +7 to +2.

questions.q: What is the main cause of the lanthanoid contraction?
questions.explain: 4f electrons shield one another poorly; so as Z increases the nuclear attraction grows and the size falls.

questions.q: Why are the radii of Zr (160 pm) and Hf (159 pm) almost equal?
options: Both have the same number of electrons
They are not in the same group
questions.explain: On going from Zr to Hf the 4f orbitals are filled, and the resulting contraction cancels the normal increase in size of 5d.

questions.q: Which statement about actinoids is correct?
options: The range of oxidation states is wider than for lanthanoids, and all are radioactive
questions.explain: 5f, 6d and 7s are close in energy, so the range is wide (from +4 to +7 besides +3); all are radioactive.
